{{< include _status.qmd >}}

::: {.lede}
`python -m pipeline.run` takes the SYNTHETIC trial from raw files to this site in about 40 seconds on a laptop. Each
step writes to a local DuckDB database, and every change to a lab record goes through an
[audit trail](glossary.qmd#audit-trail){.term}.
:::

## The pipeline

<ol class="flow" aria-label="Pipeline steps, in order">
<li><b>1. Generate</b><span>A seeded generator invents 120 volunteers, 360 samples, 13 plate-reader files, and adds 13 test problems on purpose, listed in a hidden answer key. SYNTHETIC.</span></li>
<li><b>2. Load the LIMS</b><span>Volunteers, samples and custody steps go into a mini-<a class="term" href="glossary.html#lims">LIMS</a>. Each insert writes a sealed, hash-chained audit row.</span></li>
<li><b>3. Read the plates</b><span>Plate-reader files are parsed and given a SHA-256 checksum. Corrupt files are rejected and logged, not silently skipped.</span></li>
<li><b>4. Fit the curves</b><span>A <a class="term" href="glossary.html#4pl">4PL</a> curve per plate from its 8 standards; the valid range (<a class="term" href="glossary.html#lloq">LLOQ</a> to <a class="term" href="glossary.html#uloq">ULOQ</a>) is set from standards that read back within 80–120%.</span></li>
<li><b>5. Quality checks</b><span>Plate rules (fit, standards, controls, blanks) and sample rules (duplicates, range, identity). A failed plate is rejected whole.</span></li>
<li><b>6. Pick one result per sample</b><span>The latest run on an accepted plate with no blocking flag. Everything else goes on the <a class="term" href="glossary.html#reassay">re-assay</a> list.</span></li>
<li><b>7. Integrity checks</b><span>Verify the hash chain, compare every live record with its audit row, check custody gaps and late entries (<a class="term" href="glossary.html#alcoa">ALCOA+</a>).</span></li>
<li><b>8. Marts and scorecard</b><span><a class="term" href="glossary.html#dbt">dbt</a> builds the report tables and runs 111 data tests; the scorecard compares flags with the answer key.</span></li>
</ol>

Then `site/build_data.py` turns the outputs into small JSON files, and Quarto builds this static site. The browser
loads about 0.35 MB of data, with no database.

## Method, in brief

- **Antibody level.** ELISA readings ([OD](glossary.qmd#od){.term}) are turned into AU/mL with the plate's
  [4PL](glossary.qmd#4pl){.term} curve, times the dilution. Results below the LLOQ count as half the LLOQ
  (22.86 AU/mL) in averages.
- **Typical level ([GMT](glossary.qmd#gmt){.term}).** A geometric mean with a 95% [CI](glossary.qmd#ci){.term}
  (t-based, on log10 values).
- **Rise ([GMFR](glossary.qmd#gmfr){.term}).** Each volunteer's later level divided by their Day 1 level, then
  geometric-averaged. Only volunteers with both results count.
- **Response ([seroresponse](glossary.qmd#seroresponse){.term}).** At least a 4-times rise from Day 1 (or at least
  4 times the LLOQ if Day 1 was too low to measure), with an exact
  [Clopper-Pearson](glossary.qmd#clopper-pearson){.term} 95% range.
- **Full definitions** with test cases verified by hand calculation are in `docs/METRICS.md`; architecture decisions in
  `docs/team/adr/`.

## How this site is built

- **Quarto + Observable Plot**, static HTML, publishable to GitHub Pages. No server and no database in the browser.
- **Every number** is read at build time from `docs/results.json`, `data/marts/*.csv` and the read-only DuckDB
  warehouse by `site/build_data.py`. The script re-checks that per-volunteer results add up to the published mart and
  that the rebuilt pre-tamper audit row reproduces its stored seal; if not, the build stops.
- **Accessibility.** Every chart has a "view as table" twin. Color is never the only signal (check and cross icons with words, filled vs
  hollow, letters on wells). Text meets WCAG AA contrast in light and dark mode. Animation respects
  "reduce motion", the play button has pause, and everything works with the keyboard.
- **Rebuild:** `.venv\Scripts\python -m pipeline.run`, then `.venv\Scripts\python site\build_data.py`, then
  `quarto render site`.

## Image, type and icon credits {#credits}

The site has its own look, called SPECIMEN: lab-notebook paper, a fixative-teal ink, and the 96-well plate as its
mark. Every picture slot is listed here. **No image or video has been downloaded yet.** Each slot is empty and shows
a placeholder drawn by code until Michael approves a specific public-domain file.

::: {.table-scroll}
| Slot | Where | Status now | Planned source | Credit line to use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hero-micrograph` | Overview, next to the verdict | Empty. Shows a slow, code-drawn field of cells, labelled on screen as not a real micrograph | NIAID image library (Flickr), public-domain items only; check each image, as some older uploads are CC BY 2.0 | "Image: NIAID" plus the image title and link |
| `hero-loop` (optional) | Same figure, as a 6–12 s muted loop | Empty. Would be made from the approved still with a slow pan, no audio, under 1.5 MB | Same still as above | Same as above |

: Picture slots and their sources {.credits-table}
:::

- **Type:** [Fraunces](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Fraunces) (headlines), [IBM Plex Sans](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/IBM+Plex+Sans)
  (text) and [IBM Plex Mono](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/IBM+Plex+Mono) (numbers and well IDs), served by Google
  Fonts under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.
- **Icons:** drawn inline in the page from the geometry of [Phosphor Icons](https://github.com/phosphor-icons/homepage)
  (regular weight), MIT License, © Phosphor Icons. Every icon sits next to a word; none carries meaning alone.
- **Texture:** the paper grain and the specimen field are generated in the browser (SVG noise and a small canvas
  drawing). No image files.
- **Motion:** the specimen field drifts a few pixels a second, stops when it is off-screen, has a **Pause motion**
  button, and is a still picture under your system's "reduce motion" setting. Nothing moves behind a chart, table or
  number.

## Honesty notes

::: {.honest}
- **SYNTHETIC data.** No real volunteer, trial, lab, company or patient. The assay ("Anti-Antigen X IgG ELISA") is
  invented.
- **Not a validated system.** This is a demonstration of [GxP](glossary.qmd#gxp){.term}-style practice.
  It makes no [21 CFR Part 11](glossary.qmd#part-11){.term} or [GCLP](glossary.qmd#gclp){.term} compliance claim.
  The validation pack in `docs/validation/` is a practice exercise.
- **Demo thresholds.** QC limits in `config/qc_rules.yaml` are demo defaults, not checked against any real assay
  method or ICH M10.
- **Detection, not prevention.** Anyone with the database file can edit it; the checks only detect edits.
- **Self-graded.** The same team added the test problems and wrote the checks. 13 of 13 shows the checks work as
  designed, not that they would catch every real error.
- **Numbers are truncated, never rounded up**, in headlines; tables show more decimals.
:::
